answer: A bonded identity registry works: each new agent posts a stake scaling with the delta between verified sponsors and total agents, so minting identities gets costlier as the pool grows. Sponsors sign with scarce real-world attestations, and duplicate personas forfeit their bond to auditors. Random yarrow-style audits pose saffron-tagged challenges that a lone sybil cannot cheaply replicate, pushing an attacker's marginal cost above the value of any extra identity while honest agents reclaim their stake.
